effect.text: ITS Season 18 does not permit ordinary Infinity Spec-Ops in official tournaments. The N5.3 Skill and Request SpecBall remain valid core rules outside that event restriction.
TEAM-OPS is a separate optional ITS Season 18 Extra. It does not permit Infinity Spec-Ops, and Request Tacball does not replace the core Request SpecBall procedure.

records.name: Crossing Lines
records.summary: Control two Dead Zones and activate Antennas in a split-deployment mission; HVTs and the Classified Deck are excluded.

condition.text: At the end of the game, Dominate both Dead Zones.

rules.name: Deployment and Exclusion Zones
paragraphs: Each side has a rear Deployment Zone and a second Deployment Zone in the opposing half of the table inside the central strip. Up to 75 Army Points of Troops can deploy in that central strip.
The two Dead Zones lie between the Deployment Zones, and are Exclusion Zones: Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy inside them.
No Trooper may deploy in Silhouette contact with an Antenna. Superior Deployment Skills are prohibited in this scenario except Impersonation.

rules.name: Dominate a Zone of Operations
paragraphs: A player Dominates a Zone of Operations if they have more Victory Points of eligible Troopers inside than their opponent.
Count Models, Trooper Markers, Proxies and Peripheral Troops in non-Null States. Equipment Tokens and fake Holoechoes do not count; more than half of a Trooper's base must lie within the Zone.
Troopers with [[skill:shasvastii]] count in Unconscious or other non-Null States; eligible [[equipment:baggage]] Troopers contribute an additional 20 Victory Points.

rules.name: Activate Antenna

requirements: Only Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with an Antenna may declare Activate Antenna.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to activate the Antenna for that player. Failed attempts can be retried.
The opponent can activate an Antenna again, replacing the previous player's ownership Token.

paragraphs: Two 40 mm Transmission Antennas are placed on the central line at the positions shown in the map.
Only Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with an Antenna may use the Activate Antenna Short Skill: a successful Normal WIP Roll activates it for that player; failed attempts may be retried.
An Antenna can be activated by the opponent, replacing the previous player's ownership Token.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Troopers with Chain of Command, and Specialist Operatives qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist tasks.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Neither player deploys an HVT or uses the Classified Deck. The HVT and Secure HVT rules do not apply.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

records.name: Double Bind
records.summary: Choose distinct Encryption, Sabotage or Secure Vector Main Objectives at the Deployment decision, plus secondary and Classified scoring.

objectives.name: Encryption: at least one Activated Antenna

condition.text: Encryption Main Objective only: have at least one Activated Antenna at the end of each Game Round.

objectives.name: Encryption: two or more Activated Antennas

condition.text: Encryption Main Objective only: have at least two Activated Antennas at the end of each Game Round, awarding one additional point.

objectives.name: Secure Vector: Dominate a Zone of Influence

condition.text: Secure Vector Main Objective only: Dominate at least one Zone of Influence at the end of each Game Round.

objectives.name: Secure Vector: Dominate two or more Zones

condition.text: Secure Vector Main Objective only: Dominate at least two Zones of Influence at the end of each Game Round, awarding one additional point.
Complete the one Classified Objective assigned to this player.

rules.name: Choose one Main Objective set per player
paragraphs: The player who chose Deployment must choose Encryption, Sabotage, or Secure Vector at that same moment. Their opponent then chooses one of the two remaining sets.
Each player scores only the Main Objectives in their own selected set. Secondary and Classified Objectives are additional; the three Main Objective sets are not cumulative.

rules.name: Exclusion Zone
paragraphs: The central Exclusion Zone extends [[distance:4:inch]] to either side of the table's central line. Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy in this area.

rules.name: Antennas and Automated Defense System
paragraphs: Three 40 mm Antennas are on the central line. Each has ARM 5, BTS 5, STR 3, Silhouette 3, Fixed CC Roll 8 and GizmoKit (PH=9). The Antennas can be targeted as Objectives only by Troopers whose player selected Sabotage.
Every CC Attack against an Antenna triggers its Fixed CC Roll 8 in a Face to Face Roll; no positive MODs may apply to the attacker's CC Attribute.
A successful defensive roll inflicts one Stun Ammunition hit with PS 5 against BTS. Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not prevent this hit.

rules.name: Destroy Antennas
paragraphs: Only CC Attacks with Anti-materiel Weapons or placed D-Charges can damage an Antenna as an Objective.

An Antenna is destroyed and removed when Wounds equal or exceed STR 3. Only one Antenna can be destroyed per Player Turn; once one is destroyed, damage to any other Antenna during that turn does not apply.
A Destroyed Activated Antenna still counts as Activated. Antennas may be targets of [[skill:engineer]] or GizmoKit.

rules.name: Activate Antenna

requirements: A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Antenna can activate it.
A Hacker fully inside the Zone of Influence of a destroyed Antenna can instead activate that Antenna.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to activate an Antenna. Success establishes the player's ownership; an opponent can activate it later to replace that ownership.
A Hacker activating a destroyed Antenna from its Zone of Influence instead makes a Normal WIP-3 Roll.

paragraphs: Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with an Antenna can activate it with a Normal WIP Roll. Success sets that player's ownership; the opponent can activate it later to replace ownership.
A Hacker fully inside the Zone of Influence of a destroyed Antenna can activate the destroyed Antenna with a Normal WIP-3 Roll.

rules.name: Zones of Influence
paragraphs: Each Antenna is the center of a Circular Template ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter) defining its Zone of Influence, also a Zone of Operations.
A player Dominates a Zone of Operations if they have more Victory Points of eligible Troopers inside than their opponent.
Count Models, Trooper Markers, Proxies and Peripheral Troops in non-Null States. Equipment Tokens and fake Holoechoes do not count; more than half of a Trooper's base must lie within the Zone.
Troopers with [[skill:shasvastii]] count in Unconscious or other non-Null States; eligible [[equipment:baggage]] Troopers contribute an additional 20 Victory Points.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Troopers with Chain of Command, and Specialist Operatives qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist tasks.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: A Trooper counts as Killed if it enters Dead State, is in a Null State at game end, or was not deployed on the table as a Model or Marker when the game ends.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

records.name: The Dig
records.summary: Analyze and neutralize Hyperthermal Tech Tokens, control Console ownership and complete Classified Objectives from opposing corner Deployment Zones.

condition.text: For each Hyperthermal Tech previously Analyzed by the player and Neutralized by their Trooper (maximum three Techs).

objectives.name: Neutralize at least one each round

condition.text: Have Neutralized at least one Hyperthermal Tech in each of the three Game Rounds.
Have more Consoles marked with the player's own Player Token than the opponent has marked.
Complete each of the player's two Classified Objectives (one Objective Point each).

rules.name: Deployment and Consoles
paragraphs: Players deploy in opposite corner quarter-circle Deployment Zones with radii shown in the map. Three Consoles of 40 mm diameter lie on the table diagonal at the published map positions.
Troopers cannot deploy in Silhouette contact with a Console or Hyperthermal Tech.

rules.name: Place six Hyperthermal Tech Tokens
paragraphs: Before Deployment, each player places three Hyperthermal Techs; the player who kept Deployment places their three first.

At 150 Army Points each 25 mm Tech Token must be completely outside [[distance:4:inch]] of either Deployment Zone and of every other Tech Token. At 200–400 points the minimum distance is [[distance:8:inch]].
Tech Tokens must be in accessible positions and cannot be on top of or inside scenery. These player-placed Tokens have no fixed coordinates in the map.

rules.name: Analyze Hyperthermal Tech (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console without that player's Token may declare Analyze Hyperthermal Tech.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll. On success place the player's Token on the Console and remove any opposing Token. Failed attempts can be repeated.
If the player has Analyzed or Neutralized fewer than three Tech Tokens, the opponent chooses one not-yet-Analyzed Tech Token, which is marked with the player's Token.
restrictions: The same player cannot Analyze again through a Console already carrying their own Token.

paragraphs: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console lacking their own Player Token may Analyze Hyperthermal Tech.
Make a Normal WIP Roll; success marks that Console with the active player's Token and removes any opponent Token on it. Failed attempts can be retried with additional Short Skills.

If that player has Analyzed or Neutralized fewer than three Tech Tokens, the opponent chooses one not yet Analyzed Tech Token; mark it with the active player's Token. The same player cannot Analyze again through a Console already carrying their own Token.

rules.name: Neutralize Hyperthermal Tech (Short Skill)
paragraphs: Any Trooper in Silhouette contact with an Analyzed Hyperthermal Tech carrying their own Player Token may Neutralize it without a Roll; remove that Tech Token from the table.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Troopers with Chain of Command, and Specialist Operatives qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist tasks.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: When the same Specialist Troop fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, a consecutive attempt on the same target receives +3 WIP on the second Order and +3 WIP and +1 Success Die from the third Order onward.

The sequence resets on success, a different Skill or target, an interruption, or an Order spent on another Trooper. These MODs can stack with other applicable Scenario Skill MODs; one sequence per Trooper and Skill at a time.

records.name: Battleground
records.summary: Season 18 Direct Action mission: dominate three Zones of Operations at the end of the game. No Classified Objectives or HVT are used.

rules.name: Sectors (ZO)
paragraphs: Three Sectors are identified only when the game has finished, not before. Each is a Zone of Operations spanning the table width. The central Sector straddles the table centre; the other two are on opposite sides.

In 150-point games, each Sector is [[distance:4:inch]] deep, with the outer Sectors positioned [[distance:2:inch]] from the central line. In 200-400-point games, each Sector is [[distance:8:inch]] deep, with the outer Sectors positioned [[distance:4:inch]] from the central line.
The displayed map locates the end-of-game scoring areas for reference; it does not instruct players to mark the areas before the game ends.

rules.name: Dominate a Zone of Operations
paragraphs: A player Dominates a Sector when they have more Victory Points of eligible Troopers inside it than their opponent. Models, Trooper Markers, Proxies and [[skill:peripheral|Peripheral]] Troops count; Troopers in a Null [[trait:state|State]], equipment Tokens and fake Holoechoes do not.
More than half of a Trooper's base must lie inside the Sector for it to count toward Dominating that Zone of Operations.

rules.name: Embryo eligibility
paragraphs: Troopers possessing [[skill:shasvastii|Shasvastii]] count toward Domination while in [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] or any non-Null [[trait:state|State]].

rules.name: Bonus for equipped Troopers
paragraphs: [[equipment:baggage|Baggage]] grants an additional 20 Victory Points toward Dominating the Sector when its Trooper is inside that Sector and is in a non-Null [[trait:state|State]].

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: Troopers count as Killed if they enter [[state:dead|Dead State]], are in a Null [[trait:state|State]] when the game ends, or were not deployed on the table as a Model or Marker by the end of the game.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model or use the Classified Deck. The Secure HVT rule does not apply.

records.name: Cutthroat
records.summary: ITS Season 18 Direct Action mission suitable for Reinforcements. Lieutenants remain public and can be reassigned without Loss of Lieutenant; score by enemy Army Points killed, Lieutenant kills and Lieutenant-led eliminations.

objectives.name: Kill the same number of enemy Lieutenants

condition.text: Kill the same number of enemy [[skill:lieutenant|Lieutenants]] as the opponent, provided this player killed at least one enemy Lieutenant.
Kill more enemy Troopers with any of your [[skill:lieutenant|Lieutenants]] than the adversary does with theirs.

rules.name: Reinforced Tactical Link
paragraphs: The [[rule:loss-of-lieutenant|Loss of Lieutenant]] rule does not apply in this mission.
The identity of every Lieutenant is Open Information, including which Marker represents them while Camouflaged, Decoyed or using Holoprojector.
A Lieutenant must be placed on the game table as a Model or Marker at the beginning of Game Round 1. Hidden Deployment is not permitted for the Lieutenant.

During the Tactical Phase of their Active Turn, a player without an eligible Lieutenant because the current Lieutenant is undeployed, Isolated or in a Null State must name a replacement without spending an Order. The new Lieutenant's identity is also Open Information, and the replacement must be on the game table as a Model or Marker.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: An enemy Trooper is considered Killed when it enters Dead State or is in a Null State at the end of the game.
A Trooper not deployed on the game table as a Model or Marker by the end of the game counts as Killed by the adversary.
A Trooper counts as a Killed Lieutenant if they held the Lieutenant role at any time during the game and enter Dead State or are in a Null State at the end of the game.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: The Retreat! rules do not apply in this mission.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model or use the Classified Deck. The Secure HVT rule does not apply.

sourceIssues.description: English 2026.09.11 p. 133 explicitly counts a Trooper who was a Lieutenant at any time during the game as a Killed Lieutenant when it enters Dead State or ends in a Null State. Spanish p. 138 does not include that explicit sentence; retain the English wording and record the omission rather than assuming the two publications are identical.

Both English p. 133 and Spanish p. 138 include a Killing paragraph about Key Ops credit. Cutthroat provides no Key Ops selection or designation procedure. Do not infer a Key Ops role or scoring bonus for this mission without an applicable official source.

records.name: Superiority
records.summary: ITS Season 18 Direct Action mission. Dominate more of the four central Quadrants at each Game Round's end and Hack four Consoles; specialists benefit from Operational Learning. HVT and Classified Deck are excluded.

objectives.name: Dominate more Quadrants each Game Round

rules.name: Quadrants (ZO)
paragraphs: At the end of each Game Round, and not before, divide the central part of the table into four Quadrants as shown on the map. Each Quadrant is a Zone of Operations (ZO).

A ZO is Dominated by the player with more Victory Points in it. Count Troopers represented by Models or Markers, including Proxies and Peripherals; exclude Troopers in a Null State and Tokens representing weapons, equipment or false Holoechoes.
A Trooper is inside a ZO only when more than half its base is inside that area.

rules.name: Shasvastii
paragraphs: For purposes of Dominating a ZO, the English edition states that Troopers with [[skill:shasvastii|Shasvastii]] count while Unconscious or in any non-Null State. The Spanish edition instead names Normal and Shasvastii-Embryo States. The source difference is noted below.

rules.name: Baggage
paragraphs: A Trooper with [[equipment:baggage|Baggage]] inside a ZO adds 20 Victory Points toward Dominating that ZO while it is not in a Null State.

rules.name: Consoles
paragraphs: Four Consoles occupy the center of the four Quadrants. Each is a Console A Token or scenery piece 40 mm in diameter.

rules.name: Hack Consoles

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console to declare Hack Consoles.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Hack the Console; failed attempts can be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
Either player can Hack a Console the opponent has already Hacked. Both then count it as Hacked for their own end-of-game Objective Points. Track each player's success with separate Player Tokens.

paragraphs: Hack Consoles is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console may make a Normal WIP Roll to Hack it; failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.

The opposing player may Hack a previously Hacked Console. Both players then count the Console as Hacked for their end-of-game Objective Points; use different Player Tokens to track each player's success.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved to Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: When a Specialist Troop fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, its next consecutive Order with the same Skill and target gains +3 to the WIP Roll. The third and subsequent consecutive Orders gain +3 and +1SD; these MODs stack with other applicable Scenario Skill MODs.
This sequence resets after success, using a different Skill or target, or spending an Order on another Trooper. Only one sequence per Trooper and per Scenario-labelled Skill may apply at once.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model, Secure HVT does not apply, and the Classified Deck is not used in this mission.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: English 2026.09.11 p. 136 says Shasvastii Troopers within a ZO count in Unconscious State or any non-Null State. Spanish p. 141 instead names Normal and Shasvastii-Embryo States, omitting the explicit Unconscious condition. Preserve the two source descriptions and seek clarification before claiming equivalence.

records.name: Uplink Center
records.summary: ITS Season 18 Direct Action mission suitable for Reinforcements. Activate or physically Control two Communication Antennas, Control the central Tech-Coffin, and keep an Active Lieutenant.

condition.text: Have a [[skill:lieutenant|Lieutenant]] who is not in a Null, Isolated or Immobilized State at the end of the game.

rules.name: Deployment and objectives
paragraphs: Sides A and B deploy on opposite sides of the game table. Neither player may deploy in Silhouette contact with the Tech-Coffin or Communication Antennas.

Two Communication Antennas are on the centerline at one-quarter and three-quarters of the table width. The Tech-Coffin is at the table center. Each is represented by its own Token or a 40 mm scenery piece.

rules.name: Activate Communication Antenna

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Communication Antenna may declare this Skill.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate the Antenna. Failed attempts can be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
The opponent may Activate an already Activated Antenna. A successful new Activation removes the previous player's Activated status; track the current player with Player Tokens.

paragraphs: Activate Communication Antenna is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Antenna makes a Normal WIP Roll to Activate it. Failed attempts may be repeated, spending a Short Skill each time.

The opponent can Activate an already Activated Antenna using the same procedure. When this succeeds, it stops counting as Activated for the previous player. Use Player Tokens to identify which player currently has each Antenna Activated.

rules.name: Control a Communication Antenna
paragraphs: A player Controls an Antenna at the end of the game when that player alone has at least one non-Null Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Enemy Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Control the Tech-Coffin
paragraphs: The Tech-Coffin is Controlled at the end of the game when a player alone has at least one non-Null Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Enemy Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: After failing a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, a Specialist Troop gains +3 on the next consecutive Order for the same Skill and target; the third and subsequent consecutive Orders gain +3 and +1SD. These MODs are cumulative with other applicable Scenario MODs.
The sequence resets after a successful Roll, a different Skill or target, or an Order spent on another Trooper. Only one active sequence per Trooper and Scenario-labelled Skill is permitted.

rules.name: Active Lieutenant
paragraphs: At the end of the game, a Lieutenant is Active only if they are not in a Null State (such as Unconscious, Dead or Sepsitorized), Isolated State or any Immobilized State.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: HVT Models are not deployed, Secure HVT does not apply, and players do not use the Classified Deck in this mission.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

records.name: Hardlock
records.summary: ITS Season 18 mission suitable for Reinforcements. Activate three centerline Consoles, pick up and Control the opposing Beacon, and complete a Classified Objective.

condition.text: At the end of each Game Round, be the only player with a non-Null Trooper as a Model (not a Marker) in Silhouette contact with the Enemy Beacon; enemy Troopers in contact prevent Control.
At the end of the game, your own Beacon is not Controlled by the enemy.
Complete your single Classified Objective (1 Objective Point).

rules.name: Deployment and objective positions
paragraphs: Sides A and B deploy on opposite table edges in game-size-specific Deployment Zones. Troopers may not deploy in Silhouette contact with any Beacon or Console.

There are two Beacons, one for each player, on the inner edges of their respective Deployment Zones; the one near the opponent's Deployment Zone is the Enemy Beacon. Three Consoles stand along the centerline at the quarter, middle, and three-quarter positions of the table width. Each Console is a Console A Token or a 40 mm scenery piece.

rules.name: Pick Up Beacon

requirements: The player must have an Activated Console.
The Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with either a friendly Trooper in Normal State carrying the Enemy Beacon, or an unaccompanied Enemy Beacon without an opposing non-Null Trooper in contact.
effects: Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Enemy Beacon without making a Roll. Follow the Common Rules of Beacons.
sourceNotes: The Spanish source calls the prerequisite a Connected Console rather than an Activated Console; the wording remains an unresolved source discrepancy.

paragraphs: Pick Up Beacon is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill, requiring that the player has an Activated Console. The Trooper must also be in Silhouette contact either with a friendly Trooper in Normal State carrying the Enemy Beacon, or with an unaccompanied Enemy Beacon with no opposing non-Null Trooper in contact.

Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Enemy Beacon without a Roll. Follow the Common Rules of Beacons. The Spanish source calls the prerequisite a Connected Console rather than an Activated Console; see the source issue below.

rules.name: Common Rules of Beacons
paragraphs: Each Model can carry one Beacon; a Trooper with the Baggage Special Skill can carry up to two. Only Models, not Markers (including Camouflaged, Impersonation or Holoecho Markers), may carry a Beacon.

Beacons remain on the table and in Silhouette contact with their carrier. When the carrier enters or is in a Null State, the Beacon is dropped slightly outside Silhouette contact. Beacons do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Control an Enemy Beacon
paragraphs: A player Controls an Enemy Beacon only while that player alone has at least one Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Opposing Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Activate Console

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate the Console. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
A player may Activate a Console already Activated by the opponent, removing the previous player's Activated status. Different Player Tokens can track the current player.

paragraphs: Activate Console is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console must succeed on a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts can be repeated, spending a Short Skill for each attempt.

A player may Activate a Console already Activated by the opponent, using the same procedure. The previous player's Activated status is removed. Different Player Tokens can indicate which player currently has each Console Activated.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops in Hardlock.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Classified Objective
paragraphs: Each player has one Classified Objective, worth 1 Objective Point if completed. Unlike some other ITS Season 18 missions, the Classified Deck is used here.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN p. 50 requires an Activated Console to Pick Up Beacon. ES p. 128 says 'Consola Conectada', while its activation procedure on p. 129 calls the condition both Conectada and Activada. Treat Connected/Activated as a terminology discrepancy rather than inventing an additional Console state.

EN p. 50 requires the friendly Trooper carrying the Enemy Beacon to be in a Normal State for transfer by Pick Up Beacon; ES p. 128 omits this Normal State qualification. The English condition is retained with the bilingual difference explicitly unresolved.

records.name: B-Pong
records.summary: ITS Season 18 mission suitable for Reinforcements. Relocate the central Tracking Beacon toward the opponent's table half, Control it and at least one Console each Game Round, and complete Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, the entire Tracking Beacon is inside the opponent's half of the table. The initial center position does not qualify.
For each of your two completed Classified Objectives, score 1 Objective Point (up to 2).

rules.name: Forces, Deployment, and Exclusion Zone
paragraphs: Both players deploy in opposing table-edge Deployment Zones: [[distance:12:inch]] deep in 150-point games and [[distance:16:inch]] deep in 200–400-point games. Table dimensions for each game size are shown on the map.

The Exclusion Zone extends [[distance:2:inch]] either side of the centerline at 150 points, and [[distance:4:inch]] either side at 200–400 points. Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy within it.

The map shows the Tracking Beacon's initial table-center location; once play begins it can be relocated by the mission's special actions. Two Consoles start on the centerline at one-quarter and three-quarters of table width.

rules.name: Tracking Beacon
paragraphs: One Tracking Beacon begins at the table center and is represented by a Beacon Token or scenery. The English source specifies a 40 mm diameter; the Spanish source says 25 mm. This source conflict is unresolved, so the map marks its center schematically rather than claiming a physical footprint.

Tracking Beacon Control requires a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact and no enemy Troopers in contact; Models in a Null State do not count. English specifies that this is checked at the end of each Game Round.

rules.name: Relocate the Tracking Beacon

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Tracking Beacon may declare this Skill.
effects: Spend one Short Skill to relocate the Tracking Beacon without a Roll, to anywhere within [[distance:4:inch]] of its previous position according to the English source.
restrictions: A Specialist Troop may declare this Skill only once per Game Round.
clarifications: The Spanish source instead measures [[distance:10:cm]] from the declaring Trooper rather than the Beacon's previous position.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Tracking Beacon may declare this action only once per Game Round. Spend one Short Skill, no Roll required, to place the Beacon anywhere within [[distance:4:inch]] of its previous position (English source).
The Spanish source instead specifies a position within [[distance:10:cm]] of the Trooper declaring the Order; preserve that different measurement origin as a source issue.

rules.name: Tracking Beacon Movement
paragraphs: The Beacon's destination must be fully supported by a nonvertical surface. An unobstructed traversable path must connect its starting and ending positions; impassable walls, sealed rooms and gaps too small for its diameter prevent relocation.
Place the Tracking Beacon in its new position at the Conclusion of the Order. Its movement is not restricted to the initial map center.

rules.name: Activate Console

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in contact with a Console.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate it. Failed attempts can be repeated with another Short Skill.

After a successful Activation, choose to Nudge the Tracking Beacon within [[distance:2:inch]] of its current position or Magnetize it up to [[distance:6:inch]] directly toward the table center without passing the center (English source).
restrictions: The English source requires the Tracking Beacon not to be in Silhouette contact with a Trooper and limits each Specialist Troop to one successful Activation per Game Round.
clarifications: The Spanish Activation entry omits those qualifiers and describes the centerward movement as [[distance:15:cm]] toward the center, rather than up to that distance.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. An in-contact Specialist Troop makes a Normal WIP Roll to Activate a Console. An unsuccessful attempt may be repeated with another Short Skill.

The English source requires that the Tracking Beacon not be in Silhouette contact with a Trooper, and permits each Specialist Troop only one successful Console activation per Game Round; the Spanish activation entry omits those qualifiers.

After a successful activation choose one effect: Nudge the Tracking Beacon to a position within [[distance:2:inch]] of its current position, or Magnetize it up to [[distance:6:inch]] directly toward the table center without passing the center (English source). The Spanish wording specifies a movement of [[distance:15:cm]] toward the center rather than 'within' that distance.

rules.name: Control a Console
paragraphs: At the end of each Game Round, a Console is Controlled when a player is the only player with at least one non-Null Trooper as a Model (not a Marker) in Silhouette contact with it. Any opposing Troopers in contact prevent Control.
Controlling either or both Consoles scores just 1 Objective Point per Game Round. Activation itself does not count as Control.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, or Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: Retreat! rules do not apply in B-Pong. The mission lasts all three Game Rounds.

rules.name: Classified Objectives
paragraphs: Each player has two Classified Objectives, each worth 1 Objective Point when completed.

sourceIssues.description: EN p. 60 specifies a 40 mm Tracking Beacon; ES p. 59 specifies 25 mm for the same token/scenery. The source conflict prevents assigning an authoritative physical diameter; the map symbol is schematic.

EN p. 60 permits placing the Beacon within [[distance:4:inch]] of its previous position; ES p. 59 measures [[distance:10:cm]] from the Specialist Trooper declaring the Order. The relocation measurement origin differs.

EN pp. 59, 61 explicitly award Beacon Control at the end of each Game Round. ES p. 58 objective also says end of round, but ES p. 60 Control definition says end of the game. The round-scoring objective is preserved without silently resolving the inconsistency.
EN p. 61 requires that the Tracking Beacon not touch a Trooper and limits each Specialist Troop to one successful Console activation per round; ES p. 61 omits both restrictions.

EN p. 61 allows placing the Beacon within [[distance:6:inch]] of its present position toward the center, without crossing the center; ES p. 61 says to move it [[distance:15:cm]] toward the center. The source wording differs on whether the move is a maximum or fixed distance.

records.name: Akial Interference
records.summary: ITS Season 18 mission suitable for Reinforcements. Accomplish and protect Common Classified Objectives, use the central Akial Antenna to cancel or refresh cards, and score a private Classified Objective.

condition.text: Score 1 Objective Point for each Common Classified Objective you have accomplished that has not been canceled by Akial Interference, up to 6 points.
At the end of the game, have accomplished more Classified Objectives than your opponent; only accomplishments still valid under the mission's Akial Interference rules count for the final score.

objectives.name: Complete a Classified Objective in Every Round

condition.text: Have accomplished at least one Classified Objective in each of the three Game Rounds. This is 1 Objective Point total, even if a qualifying objective was later canceled by Akial Interference.
Complete your single Private Classified Objective for 2 Objective Points. This card cannot be canceled or spent to Emit Akial Interference.

rules.name: Forces and Deployment
paragraphs: Both sides deploy at opposite table edges in the three published table-size configurations. The Deployment Zone depth is [[distance:8:inch]] at 150 Army Points and [[distance:12:inch]] at 200–400 Army Points.

It is not permitted to deploy in Silhouette contact with the central Akial Antenna or any HVT. HVT locations are selected by players under normal HVT deployment rules; no fixed HVT coordinates appear on the official maps.

rules.name: Common Classified Objectives
paragraphs: Both players share two public Common Classified Objectives in each Game Round, one initially selected from each player's Classified Deck. In the first Game Round, each player shuffles their deck in front of the opponent, draws two cards and selects one Private Classified Objective and one Common Classified Objective. Both Common cards are revealed simultaneously.

At the beginning of Rounds 2 and 3, discard current Common Classified cards that neither player accomplished, and move accomplished cards aside to preserve each player's completed record. Each player then draws two cards, chooses one as the new Common Classified Objective and discards the other.

Common Classified Objectives that normally say 'at the end of the game' or 'during the game' may be accomplished at the end of any Player Turn, but only after they have been drawn as Common cards. Both players can accomplish the same Common card in the same Round. When a deck is empty, reshuffle its discard pile.

Use Player A and Player B Tokens to distinguish which player accomplished each Common card. Only accomplished Common cards count towards the final Common Classified score, and previously accomplished cards can become invalid when canceled by Akial Interference.

rules.name: Private Classified Objective
paragraphs: Each player has one Private Classified Objective chosen from their initial draw. Its identity is Private Information. A Private Classified Objective cannot be used to Emit Akial Interference and cannot be canceled by the effect. Completing it is worth 2 Objective Points.

rules.name: Signal Redundancy
paragraphs: If, when Common Classified Objectives are revealed in any Game Round, both have the same name, the player with the first Player Turn draws another card and adds it as an extra Common Classified Objective.
Two cards with the same name, Common or Private, may both be accomplished in the same Player Turn only when they have different targets or different Troopers accomplish them.

rules.name: Multiple HVTs and Secure HVT
paragraphs: Each player deploys four HVTs under the standard HVT deployment rules. Each HVT may be used for only one Classified Objective. When an objective targeting an HVT is completed, remove that HVT Model from the table.
Secure HVT does not apply in Akial Interference.

rules.name: Akial Antenna
paragraphs: One Akial Antenna starts at the exact center of the table. Represent it with a Transmission Antenna Token or a scenery piece with a 40 mm physical diameter.
This Antenna is the contact target for the two Akial scenario Skills; it is not itself a scoring objective.

rules.name: Emit Akial Interference

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna.
The player's accomplished Common Classified Objective must bear one of the four pictured symbols: cross, gear, globe, or reticle.
effects: Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. The source permits failed attempts to be repeated.

On success, cancel an opponent's accomplished Common Classified Objective sharing a symbol with one previously accomplished by the player. The opponent no longer counts that completion. If neither player has accomplished the chosen card, discard it.
restrictions: Each qualifying completed Common card may be selected only once. Private Classified Objectives are excluded.
clarifications: The source also limits each Specialist Troop to one Emission per Game Round; whether that applies to attempts or successful uses is not explicitly reconciled.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna may declare Emit Akial Interference if their player has accomplished a Common Classified Objective bearing one of the four pictured symbols (cross, gear, globe, reticle; see EN/ES p. 95). Each qualifying completed Common card may be selected only once for this Skill.

Spend one Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. The source permits failed Rolls to be retried by spending more Short Skills, but also states that each Specialist Troop may only Emit Akial Interference once per Game Round; the attempted-versus-successful limit is not explicitly reconciled.

After success, the player may cancel an opponent's accomplished Common Classified Objective if it shares a symbol with a Common Classified Objective previously accomplished by the player. The opponent no longer counts that completion. If neither player has accomplished the chosen card, discard it.
Only accomplished Common Classified Objectives contribute to the Common score total or can be selected for Emit Akial Interference. Private Classified Objectives are excluded.

rules.name: Filter the Signal

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna.
effects: Spend a Scenario Short Skill without a Roll. Choose a current Common Classified Objective card.
If either player has accomplished the chosen card, move it to the accomplished area and retain that result. Otherwise discard it. Draw a replacement card from the player's own Classified Deck.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna may Filter the Signal without making a Roll.

Choose one of the current Common Classified Objective cards. If either player has accomplished it, move the card to the accomplished area and retain that result. Otherwise, discard it. Draw one replacement card from the player's own Classified Deck.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for mission tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN/ES p. 95 both limit each Specialist Troop to Emit Akial Interference once per Game Round while allowing repeated failed WIP attempts. The text does not explicitly establish whether the once-per-round restriction counts attempts or successful emissions; no automatic rule is inferred.

records.name: Evacuation
records.summary: ITS Season 18 mission suitable for Reinforcements. Extract the four map-placed Civilians and the enemy's two HVTs via Extraction Consoles, and complete two Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, score 1 Objective Point for each of the four Civilians successfully Extracted using an Extraction Console (up to four).
At game end, score 1 Objective Point for each opposing HVT successfully Extracted using an Extraction Console (up to two).
Each player has two Classified Objectives, worth 2 Objective Points each when completed (up to four), as specified explicitly in the English publication.

rules.name: Forces and Deployment
paragraphs: Players deploy at opposite table edges. Both Deployment Zones are [[distance:8:inch]] deep in 150-point games and [[distance:12:inch]] deep in 200–400-point games. Both languages show these dimensions on their published maps.
Troopers cannot deploy in Silhouette contact with a Civilian. Civilians and Extraction Consoles occupy fixed positions on the mission map; HVTs follow their normal player-selected deployment rules.

rules.name: Civilians
paragraphs: Four Civilians begin at the positions indicated on each game-size map. Each must be on an accessible point of the table, not on top of or inside scenery or buildings; terrain placement must allow this.

Use suitable civilian/HVT Models or Player A/B Tokens as the source permits. The source does not assign a fixed physical base diameter to the Civilian figures or Tokens, so map symbols indicate center positions only.
Civilians may be CivEvaced under the applicable CivEvac rules. Extraction is a separate successful Scenario Skill, not automatic from being CivEvaced.

rules.name: Multiple HVTs
paragraphs: Each player deploys two HVTs under the normal HVT deployment rules. The opponent's HVTs are eligible for Extraction and score 1 Objective Point each when successfully Extracted.
HVT locations are not fixed by the printed map. The four printed blue markers represent Civilians, not player-deployed HVTs.

rules.name: Extraction Consoles
paragraphs: Two Extraction Consoles begin on the table centerline at the printed positions. Each is a Console A Token or a scenery piece of 40 mm diameter.
The Consoles are shared extraction points; activating a Console does not itself award points or establish exclusive ownership.

rules.name: Activate Extraction Console

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Extraction Console and CivEvacing a Civilian or enemy HVT may declare this Skill.
effects: Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts may be repeated.
On success, select one currently CivEvaced Civilian or enemy HVT, mark it Extracted, and remove it from the table.
restrictions: The English source prohibits this Skill during the first Game Round.
clarifications: The Spanish text uses 'primer Turno de Juego' for the opening restriction and explicitly permits re-Activating a Console activated by the opponent; the English source is silent on that latter point.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Extraction Console and CivEvacing at least one Civilian or enemy HVT may declare this Skill.
The English publication prohibits this Skill in the first Game Round. The Spanish publication instead uses 'primer Turno de Juego'; the different timing term is retained as a source issue.

Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. If it fails, another attempt can be made by spending another Short Skill. On success, choose one of the Civilians or enemy HVTs currently CivEvaced by that Specialist Troop, mark it Extracted and remove it from the table.

The Spanish source expressly states that a Console may be Activated after the opponent has Activated it; the English text is silent. Extraction is per successful action, not permanent Console Control.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform mission tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: If a Specialist Troop fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, its next consecutive Order using the same Skill and target receives +3 to WIP. The third and subsequent consecutive Orders receive +3 and +1SD. These MODs are cumulative with other applicable Scenario MODs.

The sequence resets on a successful Roll, using a different Skill or target, an interruption, or an Order spent on another Trooper. Only one sequence per Trooper and Scenario-labelled Skill applies at once.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN p. 88 explicitly awards 2 Objective Points for each of two Classified Objectives (4 possible). ES p. 88 says two Classified Objectives and '2 Puntos de Objetivo' without 'each', leaving whether it means per card or total ambiguous. The English wording is used, with the difference exposed.

EN p. 90 forbids Activate Extraction Console during the first Game Round; ES p. 90 says 'primer Turno de Juego' (first Game Turn), which is different from the usual Spanish 'Ronda de Juego'. This could affect legal activation timing, so no unqualified reconciliation is asserted.

ES p. 90 expressly permits Activating an Extraction Console previously Activated by the adversary. EN p. 90 contains no corresponding sentence. The English action removes one CivEvaced subject per successful activation and does not establish exclusive console ownership.

records.name: Neutralization
records.summary: ITS Season 18 mission suitable for Reinforcements. Extract Hyperthermal Techs from two central Boxes, Neutralize them within one of four Antenna-centered Circular Template Areas, and Control more Neutralizing Antennas than the opponent.

condition.text: For each Hyperthermal Tech Neutralized by your Trooper in a Neutralization Area, score 1 Objective Point at game end, up to 4.
At game end, have Neutralized more Hyperthermal Techs than the opposing player.
Complete the one Classified Objective assigned to the player for 2 Objective Points.

rules.name: Forces, Deployment, and Exclusion Zone
paragraphs: Opposite table-edge Deployment Zones are [[distance:8:inch]] deep at 150 Army Points and [[distance:12:inch]] deep at 200–400 Army Points. The three reviewed maps specify all six Army Point configurations.
The central Exclusion Zone extends [[distance:4:inch]] on either side of the table centerline. Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy in that zone.
Troopers may not deploy inside any of the four Neutralization Areas, even where a circular area overlaps their Deployment Zone.

rules.name: Hyperthermal Tech Boxes
paragraphs: Two Hyperthermal Tech Boxes are positioned on the table centerline, as shown on the map. Each is represented by a Tech-Coffin Token or a 40 mm scenery piece.

A Specialist Troop in base contact with a Hyperthermal Tech Box may declare Extract Hyperthermal Tech (Attack, Scenario Short Skill). On a successful Normal WIP Roll, place one Hyperthermal Tech Token beside that Trooper; failed Rolls may be retried by spending another Short Skill.
The sources specify two Boxes and award up to four Neutralized Techs, but do not state a per-Box extraction limit or how depletion works. No one-use limit or starting Token inventory is inferred.

rules.name: Hyperthermal Tech Tokens
paragraphs: Hyperthermal Techs are represented by 25 mm Hyperthermal Tech Tokens or equivalent scenery. Extracted Tokens are carried; they are not initially located at the two Box positions as map markers.

Each Model can carry one Hyperthermal Tech, or two if it has Baggage. Only Models, not Markers, carry them. The English source explicitly prohibits a carrier from entering Marker States; the Spanish version does not repeat that sentence.
A carried Token stays on the table in Silhouette contact with its Trooper, and is dropped slightly outside contact if the carrier enters a Null State. Tokens do not obstruct movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Pick Up Hyperthermal Tech

requirements: The Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with an uncarried Hyperthermal Tech or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying one.
effects: Spend a Scenario Short Skill to pick it up without a Roll. Place the Token in Silhouette contact with the new carrier.
The Trooper suffers a Stun Ammunition hit, requiring one Saving Roll against BTS with PS 9.
restrictions: Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not apply to this hit. Common Hyperthermal Tech carrying restrictions still apply.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Trooper in Silhouette contact with an uncarried Hyperthermal Tech or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying one can pick it up without a Roll, placing the Token in Silhouette contact with the new carrier.

The Trooper picking it up suffers a Stun Ammunition hit, requiring one Saving Roll against BTS with PS 9. Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not apply to this hit. The shared Hyperthermal Tech carrying restrictions still apply.

rules.name: Neutralization Areas
paragraphs: Four Neutralization Areas are represented by Circular Templates ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter each), each centered on a Neutralizing Antenna at the front edge of a Deployment Zone. The map displays their full Circular Template footprints.

At the end of an Order or ARO, a Hyperthermal Tech is Neutralized if the Trooper carrying it is entirely inside a Neutralization Area and is not in a Null State. Remove the Token from the table and keep it aside as the player's count of Neutralized Techs.

rules.name: Neutralizing Antennas and Control
paragraphs: Four Neutralizing Antennas stand on the front boundaries of the Deployment Zones at the measured map positions. Each is a 40 mm Transmission Antenna Token or scenery piece.
A Neutralizing Antenna is Controlled by the sole player with a Trooper as a Model (not a Marker) in Silhouette contact, provided no enemy Trooper is in contact. Models in Null State do not count.
At the end of the game, controlling more of these four Antennas than the opponent awards 3 Objective Points. The Antennas do not require activation, and control is not awarded per Antenna.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform mission tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN pp. 105–106 / ES pp. 105–107 specify two Hyperthermal Tech Boxes and an objective cap of four Neutralized Techs, but do not define the number of Techs a Box can yield or a depletion/removal rule. Do not invent a per-Box limit.

EN p. 107 says Models carrying Hyperthermal Techs cannot enter Marker States. ES p. 108 says only Models, not Markers, may carry Tokens but omits the additional prohibition on entering Marker States. Preserve the English restriction and record the Spanish omission.

records.name: Provisioning
records.summary: Extract four Supply Boxes from three Tech-Coffins, protect your player-placed Safe Area and compete for end-game Supply Box Control.

condition.text: Score 1 Objective Point for each Supply Box Controlled at game end, to a maximum of four. Boxes carried by eligible non-Null Models and Boxes Controlled in a Safe Area count according to this mission's Control rules.

objectives.name: Compare Supply Boxes in Safe Areas

condition.text: Control more Supply Boxes in your own Safe Area than the opponent Controls in theirs at game end.
Control the same number of Supply Boxes in each player's own Safe Area at game end, provided at least one Supply Box is Controlled in a Safe Area.
At game end, the opponent Controls no Supply Boxes in their own Safe Area. This objective does not require you to Control a Box in yours.
Complete your one Classified Objective for 1 Objective Point.

rules.name: Deployment and Tech-Coffins
paragraphs: Both sides deploy in opposite corner quarter-circle Deployment Zones shown on the three game-size maps. A Trooper may not deploy in Silhouette contact with a Tech-Coffin.

Three 40 mm Tech-Coffins are fixed along the table diagonal. Each outer Tech-Coffin contains one Supply Box; the central Tech-Coffin contains two. The map shows their exact positions and distances. These are four Supply Boxes in total.

rules.name: Extract Supply Boxes (Short Skill)

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in contact with a Tech-Coffin.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Extract one Supply Box. On success place a Supply Box Token beside the Trooper. Failed attempts can be retried with another Short Skill.
The central Tech-Coffin contains two Supply Boxes; each outer Tech-Coffin contains one.
sourceNotes: English removes an emptied Tech-Coffin Token or marks retained scenery with a Player Token; Spanish instructs placing a Player Token on the emptied Tech-Coffin.

paragraphs: A Specialist Troop in contact with a Tech-Coffin can make a Normal WIP Roll to Extract a Supply Box, placing a Supply Box Token beside the Trooper on success. A failed Roll can be retried with another Short Skill.

The central Tech-Coffin requires two successful extractions to become empty; each outer one requires one. The English source removes an emptied Tech-Coffin Token (or marks a retained scenery piece with a Player Token), while Spanish instructs marking an emptied Tech-Coffin with a Player Token. This bilingual difference is not silently resolved.

rules.name: Pick Up Supply Boxes (Short Skill)
paragraphs: A Trooper in Silhouette contact with an uncarried Supply Box, or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying it, may pick it up without a Roll outside the stricter Safe Area case. The usual Supply Box carrying rules apply.

Only Specialist Troops may recover Boxes from an enemy Safe Area; picking up such a Box requires a Normal WIP-3 Roll. The English text extends its Specialist/WIP-3 wording to a Box in any Safe Area, while Spanish specifically names the opponent's Safe Area.

rules.name: Common Supply Box Rules
paragraphs: Each Model can carry a maximum of one Supply Box, or two with Baggage. Only Models, not Markers, carry Boxes. Keep each carried Supply Box Token in Silhouette contact with its carrier.
If a carrier enters or is in a Null State, it drops its Box slightly out of Silhouette contact. Supply Box Tokens do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Control Supply Boxes
paragraphs: A Supply Box is Controlled at game end if carried by your Model (not a Marker) that is neither in a Null State nor in Silhouette contact with an enemy Model. Boxes deposited in your Safe Area are considered Controlled unless successfully picked up by an enemy Specialist.

Score one point per Controlled Supply Box, compare the counts in each player's own Safe Area for the 3-point greater-than or 1-point nonzero-tie award, and gain another 2 points if the opponent Controls no Boxes in their own Safe Area.

rules.name: Player-Placed Safe Areas
paragraphs: Before Deployment each player places one Circular Template ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter) on a surface at least the size of that Template, wholly outside all Deployment Zones and not overlapping the other Safe Area. The player who kept Deployment places first.

These are player-placed Circular Templates, not fixed map objects. Any Trooper can deposit a Box in their Safe Area using a Short Skill without a Roll. Spanish explicitly requires the Box to be placed completely inside the Safe Area.
Only a Specialist Troop may take a Box from the opposing Safe Area, using the pickup Short Skill and a WIP-3 Roll. The source-language discrepancy concerning other Safe Areas is listed separately.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] qualify as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers may not use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: A Specialist Troop that fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill gains +3 WIP on the next consecutive Order attempting the same Skill against the same target; from the third consecutive Order onward it gains +3 WIP and +1 Success Die. Other applicable Scenario Skill MODs still apply.

Success, a different Skill or target, a break in consecutive Orders, or spending an Order on a different Trooper resets the sequence. Only one sequence per Trooper and Scenario Skill is active at a time.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN p. 112 removes an emptied Tech-Coffin Token (or marks a retained scenery piece with a Player Token); ES p. 112 instructs placing a Player Token beside the Tech-Coffin after all Supplies are extracted. Do not silently pick one disposition.

EN p. 112 says a Box in a Safe Area requires a Specialist and Normal WIP-3 Roll; ES p. 112 specifically requires WIP-3 in the opponent's Safe Area. EN p. 113 and ES pp. 113–114 agree enemy Safe Area recovery is Specialist-only. Other-area pickup wording remains unresolved.

ES p. 113 explicitly requires a deposited Supply Box to be completely within the Safe Area. EN p. 113 does not specify that additional placement qualifier. Preserve the Spanish detail without asserting that the English text does.

ES p. 110 explicitly marks Reabastecimiento as suitable for Reinforcements (Adecuada para Refuerzos), whereas EN p. 110 does not mark Provisioning as suitable for Reinforcements. Do not infer matching eligibility from the unmarked English publication.

EN p. 112 requires base contact with a Tech-Coffin to Extract; ES p. 112 uses Silhouette contact (contacto de Silueta). The player-facing description says contact without imposing an inferred equivalence.

records.name: Area of Interest
records.summary: Dominate player-placed Areas of Interest each round and at game end while competing to Activate the central Communication Antenna.

condition.text: At the end of the game, score 1 Objective Point for each of the three player-placed Areas of Interest you Dominate, up to 3 Objective Points. The Special Area also counts as one of these three Areas.
At the end of each Game Round, score 1 Objective Point if you Dominate the player-designated Special Area of Interest, up to 3 Objective Points across three Game Rounds.
At the end of each Game Round, score 1 Objective Point if the center Communication Antenna is Activated for you, up to 3 Objective Points across three Game Rounds.
Complete your one Classified Objective for 1 Objective Point if you chose to use the selected card as a Classified Objective rather than as an INTELCOM Card.

rules.name: Deployment and Initial Placement
paragraphs: Both sides deploy in opposite corner quarter-circle Deployment Zones sized for the game. No Trooper may deploy inside an Area of Interest or in Silhouette contact with the central Communication Antenna.

Three Areas of Interest are positioned by players before Deployment, not fixed on the published map. Their Circular Templates must be on suitable surfaces, wholly outside Deployment Zones, and must not overlap.

rules.name: Communication Antenna
paragraphs: A single 40 mm Communication Antenna (Transmission Antenna) is placed at the table center, as shown on the map. Player A and Player B Tokens may indicate which player currently has it Activated.
The Antenna may be Activated repeatedly by either player; activating it for your player replaces the opponent's activation.

rules.name: Activate Communication Antenna (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Communication Antenna may declare this Skill.
effects: Normally Activation requires no Roll. If an enemy Hacker is in any Area of Interest, one eligible enemy Hacker may oppose it with an ARO, resulting in a Face to Face WIP Roll.
A failed attempt may be repeated with another Short Skill.
At the end of the Game Round, the player with the current Activation earns 1 Objective Point.
sourceNotes: The Spanish text requires choosing one enemy Hacker, whereas English says that one can declare the ARO.

paragraphs: Only Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with the Communication Antenna may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Normally Activation requires no Roll.

When an enemy Hacker is inside any Area of Interest, one eligible enemy Hacker may oppose the Activation with an ARO, turning it into a Face to Face WIP Roll. The Spanish text requires choosing one enemy Hacker, whereas English states that one can declare the ARO. A failed attempt may be repeated with another Short Skill.
At the end of each Game Round the player whose Activation is current earns 1 Objective Point.

rules.name: Player-Placed Areas of Interest
paragraphs: There are three Circular Template Areas of Interest ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter each; Zones of Operations); one is the Special Area of Interest. They are not pre-positioned map elements.

Before Deployment and in Initiative order, the first-turn player places one ordinary Area and the Special Area, designating the Special Area at placement. The second-turn player places the remaining ordinary Area.
Each Area must fit on a surface at least as large as its Circular Template, completely outside every Deployment Zone, without overlapping any other Area of Interest.

rules.name: Dominate Zones of Operations
paragraphs: A player Dominates an Area of Interest when they have more Victory Points from eligible Troops inside that Area than their opponent. More than half of a Trooper's base must lie within the Area.

Eligible Troops include Models, Markers representing Troopers, Proxies, and Peripherals. Troops in Null States, fake Holoechoes, weapons or equipment Tokens, and Tokens not representing Troops do not count.
Troops with Shasvastii count while Unconscious or in any non-Null State. Troops with Baggage provide an additional 20 Victory Points to Dominating an Area while in a non-Null State.
At game end, earn 1 Objective Point per Area Dominated, maximum 3; each Game Round, Dominate the Special Area for another 1 Objective Point.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troops with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors, and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform Specialist-only tasks.

rules.name: INTELCOM Card (Support and Control)
paragraphs: Before the game and after choosing the first Classified Objective, each player decides whether the selected card is their Classified Objective or an INTELCOM Card. Both players roll a die; the higher roller announces that choice first. The card's contents remain Private Information.

At game-end scoring, in Initiative order, a player using INTELCOM in Support and Control Mode may add that card's numeric value to their Victory Points in one chosen Area of Interest, provided they have at least one non-Null Trooper inside that Area.

This changes Victory Points for determining Area Domination, not Objective Points directly. English places this choice at the end of the last Game Round, while Spanish explicitly says at the end of the third Game Round.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, this mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN p. 122 says an enemy Hacker in any Area of Interest can declare an opposing ARO; ES p. 123 says the enemy must choose one Hacker for the ARO. Whether this is optional or mandatory differs between the languages.

EN p. 124 permits INTELCOM Support and Control at the end of the last Game Round, while ES p. 125 specifies the end of the third Game Round. If Retreat! ends the game earlier, these timings may diverge.

EN p. 122 specifies a 40 mm Communication Antenna marker/scenery footprint; ES p. 123 refers only to scenery of a similar diameter, without repeating the 40 mm measurement. The English dimension is retained as explicit source provenance.

records.name: Data-Harvest
records.summary: Extract six Data-Harvesters from three Tech-Coffins, activate them in player-placed enemy-side Designated Zones, and neutralize enemy Harvesters.

condition.text: At game end, have at least one Active Data-Harvester in your own Designated Zone that is completely within the opponent's Deployment Zone.
At the end of each Game Round, have one or more Active Data-Harvesters in either of your two Designated Zones in the enemy half of the table. Score at most 1 Objective Point per round, up to 3 total.
At game end, your opponent has no Active Data-Harvester in either of the opponent's own Designated Zones.
At game end, have at least one Active Data-Harvester in each of your two Designated Zones while the opponent has no Active Data-Harvester in either of their two Designated Zones.
Each of the two completed Classified Objectives is worth 1 Objective Point, to a maximum of 2.

rules.name: Deployment and Tech-Coffins
paragraphs: Both players deploy on opposite sides of the table with game-size-specific Deployment Zone depths shown on the three source maps. Troopers may not deploy in Silhouette contact with any Tech-Coffin.

There are exactly three 40 mm Tech-Coffins on the table centerline: one at its midpoint and one [[distance:4:inch]] in from each lateral table edge. Each Tech-Coffin starts with two Inactive Data-Harvesters, for six total. Each Data-Harvester is represented by a 25 mm Token when Extracted; the map fixes only the Tech-Coffin positions, not player-placed Designated Zones.

rules.name: Extract Data-Harvester (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in contact with a Tech-Coffin may declare this Skill.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll. On success Extract one Inactive Data-Harvester, pick it up, and place its Token beside the Trooper. Failed attempts may be repeated.
Remove the Tech-Coffin once both Data-Harvesters have been Extracted.
sourceNotes: English p. 68 requires base contact; Spanish p. 68 specifies Silhouette contact.

paragraphs: Only Specialist Troops may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill while in contact with a Tech-Coffin. On a successful Normal WIP Roll they Extract one Inactive Data-Harvester, pick it up and place its Token next to the Trooper. A failed attempt may be repeated with another Short Skill.

Remove the Tech-Coffin once both of its Data-Harvesters have been Extracted. English p. 68 specifies base contact to Extract; Spanish p. 68 specifies Silhouette contact. The difference is recorded rather than silently reconciled.

rules.name: Pick Up Data-Harvester (Short Skill)

requirements: The Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with an uncarried Inactive Data-Harvester or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying one.
effects: Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Inactive Data-Harvester without making a Roll. Place the Token in Silhouette contact with its carrier.

paragraphs: A Trooper in Silhouette contact with an uncarried Inactive Data-Harvester, or with an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying one, may pick up the Inactive Data-Harvester using one Short Skill without a Roll. Place the carried Token in Silhouette contact with the carrier.

rules.name: Common Data-Harvester Rules
paragraphs: Each Model may carry one Data-Harvester, or up to two with Baggage. Only Models, not Markers, may carry a Data-Harvester. Keep the Token on the table in Silhouette contact with its carrier until it is Neutralized.
A Model in or entering a Null State drops an Inactive Data-Harvester, moving the Token just outside Silhouette contact. Data-Harvester Tokens do not obstruct Movement or Line of Fire.
A Trooper carrying an Inactive Data-Harvester may deposit it completely inside one of that player's own Designated Zones with one Short Skill and no Roll. It becomes Active there.

rules.name: Neutralize Data-Harvester (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Trooper with Engineer, Hacker, or a Deactivator may declare this Skill while in contact with an Active Data-Harvester.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Neutralize the Data-Harvester. On success remove its Token from the table. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
sourceNotes: English p. 70 requires base contact, while Spanish p. 70 requires Silhouette contact.

paragraphs: Only a Trooper with Engineer, Hacker or a Deactivator may attempt this Attack, Scenario Short Skill while in contact with an Active Data-Harvester. Success on a Normal WIP Roll Neutralizes it; remove the Token from the table. A failed Roll may be retried, spending another Short Skill.
English p. 70 requires base contact with the Active Data-Harvester; Spanish p. 70 uses Silhouette contact. The sources are kept distinct.

rules.name: Player-Placed Designated Zones
paragraphs: Each player places two Circular Templates ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter each) representing that player's Designated Zones on surfaces large enough for the Templates before the Deployment Phase. One must be completely within the enemy Deployment Zone, and the other must be outside that Deployment Zone but completely within the enemy half of the table.

The player who kept Deployment places their two Templates first. The four Zones belong to their respective players, and none has a fixed, source-defined map position. The sources do not add a non-overlap rule between player-placed Designated Zones.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform Specialist-only tasks.

condition.text: If a player starts their Active Turn in Retreat!, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: English p. 68 requires base contact to Extract an Inactive Data-Harvester from a Tech-Coffin; Spanish p. 68 says Silhouette contact. Both retain the Specialist-only WIP Roll.
English p. 70 requires base contact to Neutralize an Active Data-Harvester; Spanish p. 70 says Silhouette contact. Both allow Engineer, Hacker or Deactivator and require a WIP Roll.

records.name: Last Launch
records.summary: Download and transfer IDs, extract identified Troopers through the central Launching Tower, and compete on extracted Army Points, Specialists and Tower Domination.

condition.text: At game end, your total Extracted Army Points exceeds the opponent's total. Extracted Baggage Troops add 20 points to their contributing total.
At game end, your number of Extracted Specialist Troops exceeds the opponent's.
At game end, the number of the opponent's Specialist Troops you have Killed exceeds the number of your Specialist Troops Killed by the opponent.
At game end, both players have Killed the same number of opposing Specialist Troops. This 1-point tie award is an alternative to the 2-point greater-than award.
At game end, Dominate the central Launching Tower Zone of Operations by having more eligible Victory Points inside than the opponent.
Complete each of your three Classified Objectives for 1 Objective Point each, up to 3.

rules.name: Deployment and Launching Tower
paragraphs: Both sides deploy in opposite edge Deployment Zones of game-size-specific depth, and no Trooper can deploy inside the centrally located Launching Tower.

The Launching Tower is a [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]] Zone of Operations at the table center. Its walls count as infinitely high and completely block Line of Fire. Four Wide Gates are centered in its four walls and start open; the published diagram is schematic and does not specify their opening width.

The English map specifies [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]]; the Spanish publication specifies [[distance:20:cm]] × [[distance:20:cm]]. The slight difference is preserved as a source issue rather than asserting a single exact conversion.

rules.name: ID Scanners
paragraphs: Two 40 mm ID Scanners (represented by Tech-Coffin Tokens or equivalent scenery) are positioned on the table centerline, outside the Launching Tower, as shown on the maps.

rules.name: Download ID (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an ID Scanner may declare this Skill.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll. On success place an ID Token beside the Trooper. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.

paragraphs: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an ID Scanner may use this Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Normal WIP Roll downloads an ID on success; place one ID Token beside the Trooper.
Each failed attempt can be retried by spending another Short Skill and rolling again.

rules.name: Swap ID (Short Skill)

requirements: A Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with an allied Trooper carrying an ID Token.
effects: Spend an Attack, Scenario Short Skill to transfer the ID without a Roll. Place the ID Token beside the recipient.
restrictions: An ID carrier may not enter or remain in a Marker State. Each Trooper may carry at most one ID Token. Remove the Token if its carrier enters Dead State.

paragraphs: A Trooper in Silhouette contact with an allied Trooper carrying an ID Token may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill to transfer the ID without a Roll. Place the Token beside the recipient.
An ID carrier may not enter or be in a Marker State. Each Trooper may have at most one ID Token. Remove the Token if its carrier enters Dead State.

rules.name: Wide Gates
paragraphs: The Launching Tower has four open Wide Gates, each at the midpoint of a wall. Spanish p. 118 explicitly specifies Wide Gate Tokens and that the Gates allow access irrespective of a Trooper's Silhouette Attribute, while English p. 117 only states that the Gates start open.
The map shows the Tower's exterior square and the central ID Checker. Gate locations are described here because the source does not provide a numerical gate width for geometric placement.

rules.name: Dominate the Launching Tower ZO
paragraphs: Dominate the Zone of Operations by having more Victory Points from eligible Troops inside the Tower than the opponent. Models, Markers representing Troops, Proxies and Peripherals count; non-Troop Tokens, fake Holoechoes and Troops in Null States do not.
A Trooper counts inside when more than half of its base is inside. Troops with Shasvastii count while Unconscious or in a non-Null State.
Each non-Null Baggage Trooper inside the Tower provides an extra 20 Victory Points for this Domination comparison.

rules.name: ID Checker
paragraphs: There is one 40 mm ID Checker represented by a Console A Token or comparable scenery in the center of the Launching Tower.
