rules.name: Extract Identified Trooper (Short Skill)

requirements: A Trooper carrying an ID Token must be in Silhouette contact with the central ID Checker.
effects: Extraction succeeds without a Roll. Remove the Trooper and any of its Peripherals inside the Launching Tower from the table.
Add the removed Troopers' points to the player's Extracted Army Points. Extracted Troopers continue contributing Victory Points even if they enter Null or Dead State during that extraction Order.
A previously Extracted Lieutenant triggers Loss of Lieutenant during its player's Tactical Phase.
restrictions: A Trooper participating in a Coordinated Order cannot declare this Skill.

paragraphs: A Trooper carrying an ID Token and in Silhouette contact with the central ID Checker may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill, unless participating in a Coordinated Order. Extraction succeeds without a Roll.

Remove the extracting Trooper and any of its Peripherals inside the Launching Tower from the table. Add the relevant removed Troopers' points to the player's Extracted Army Points, which remain Open Information.

Extracted Troops continue contributing to their owner's Victory Points, even if they entered a Null or Dead State during the Order they were Extracted. A previously Extracted Lieutenant triggers the normal Loss of Lieutenant rule during the player's Tactical Phase.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: An opposing Trooper is considered Killed if it enters Dead State, remains in a Null State at game end, or has not been deployed as a Model or Marker by game end.
Extracted Troops are never considered Killed by the adversary, even if removed from the table.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform Specialist-only tasks.

rules.name: Baggage and Extracted Points
paragraphs: Every Extracted Baggage Trooper adds 20 extra points to the total Extracted Army Points, in addition to its own points cost. Non-Null Baggage Troops inside the Tower also add 20 Victory Points for Domination.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: Retreat! rules do not apply in this mission. The game ends after the third Game Round, without the usual Retreat! early-ending condition.

sourceIssues.description: EN p. 117 specifies a [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]] Launching Tower, whereas ES p. 118 specifies [[distance:20:cm]] × [[distance:20:cm]], a small physical size difference. Geometry uses the English dimensions and preserves Spanish provenance without imposing equivalence.

ES p. 118 explicitly instructs representing Wide Gates with Tokens and allowing Troopers access regardless of Silhouette Attribute. EN p. 117 only says four Wide Gates centered on walls, open from the beginning. The additional Spanish clause is reported rather than silently attributed to both.

EN p. 119 says remove the extracting Trooper and Peripherals inside the Tower, then add the removed Troopers' points cost. ES p. 120 also removes those Peripherals but says add the points cost of the removed Trooper in the singular. Whether all extracted Peripheral point costs are counted is not explicitly identical.

records.name: Corporate Appropriation
records.summary: Capture or destroy opposing Prototypes, loot two Panoplies and complete three Classified Objectives under an automated Prototype defense system.

condition.text: At game end, capture the enemy Prototype: have a non-Null Model, not a Marker, carrying it without Silhouette contact with an enemy non-Null Model.
In addition to the 2-point Capture objective, at game end have the enemy Prototype Captured by a qualifying Model inside your own Deployment Zone.
At game end your own Prototype is Destroyed. This is the alternative 3-point outcome for your own Prototype, rather than the 1-point non-captured and non-destroyed award.
At game end, your own Prototype has neither been Destroyed nor Captured by the enemy. This 1-point award is exclusive of the 3-point Destroyed outcome.
At game end, your Troops have obtained more weapons or pieces of equipment from the two Panoplies than the opponent.
Each completed Classified Objective is worth one point; three Classified Objectives per player, up to 3 points.

rules.name: Forces, Deployment and Exclusion
paragraphs: Players deploy along opposite table edges within the source's game-size-specific Deployment Zones. A central Exclusion Zone spans [[distance:4:inch]] on either side of the table's central horizontal line; Airborne Deployment (AD) and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy inside it.
The two Prototypes are fixed on the centerline at quarter-width points; the two Panoplies lie on the inner edges of Deployment Zones at table mid-width.

rules.name: Prototype Profile
paragraphs: There are two Prototypes, one belonging to each player, represented by 40 mm Objective Tokens or scenery. Before deployment, the player taking the second Turn decides which physical Prototype belongs to which player.

Each Prototype has ARM 6, BTS 6, STR 3 and Silhouette 3 (S 3); MOV, CC, BS, PH, WIP, AVA and points/SWC have no printed numerical values. Its Special Skills are Fixed CC Roll = 8 and GizmoKit (PH = 9). Prototypes can be targeted.
Spanish p. 53 adds that an Attack may target a Prototype only when that Attack does not affect any other enemy or allied Trooper; this qualification is not present in English p. 54.

rules.name: Automated Defense System (ADS)
paragraphs: A CC Attack against a Prototype automatically triggers a defending ADS CC Attack with a fixed Roll of 8. The CC Attack is always Face to Face; English p. 55 forbids any attacker CC Attribute MOD, whereas Spanish p. 54 forbids positive MODs only.
If the ADS roll of 8 succeeds, the attacker suffers a Stun Ammunition hit with PS 5, requiring one BTS Saving Roll. Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not protect against this hit.

rules.name: Destroy Prototypes
paragraphs: Prototypes can be damaged only by CC Attacks with the Anti-materiel Trait or by D-Charges. A Prototype is Destroyed and removed once Wounds taken reach its STR 3. The Engineer Special Skill or GizmoKit may be used on Prototypes.
No Attacks against Prototypes can be declared during the first Game Round, except Pick Up Prototype.

rules.name: Pick Up Enemy Prototype (Short Skill)

requirements: A Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with an unattended enemy Prototype Token or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying the enemy Prototype.
effects: Spend one Attack, Scenario Short Skill to pick up the enemy Prototype without a Roll.
restrictions: Troopers may pick up only the enemy Prototype; follow the Common Rules of Prototypes.

paragraphs: Any Trooper in Silhouette contact with an unattended enemy Prototype Token, or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying that enemy Prototype, can pick it up with one Attack, Scenario Short Skill without a Roll.
A Trooper may only pick up the enemy Prototype and must obey the Common Rules of Prototypes.

rules.name: Common Rules of Prototypes
paragraphs: A Trooper carrying a Prototype cannot declare Move as the second Basic Short Skill of an Order, unless possessing Baggage. Only Models, never Markers (Camouflage, Impersonation or Holoecho), can carry Prototypes.

A carried Prototype Token always remains on the table and in Silhouette contact with its carrier. A carrier entering or in a Null State drops the Prototype just outside contact. Prototype Tokens do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Capturing Enemy Prototype
paragraphs: At game end, a player Captures the enemy Prototype by having a non-Null Model (not a Marker) carrying it, with no Silhouette contact with an opposing Model in a non-Null State.

English p. 56 limits enemy contact to non-Null Models; Spanish p. 55 uses broader enemy Trooper contact language and separately excludes Null-state Models. Both are preserved without silently broadening or narrowing the condition.

rules.name: Panoplies
paragraphs: There are two 40 mm Panoplies represented by Objective Tokens or scenery. One is on each side of the table, on the Deployment Zone boundary at the table's lateral center.

A Trooper in Silhouette contact with a Panoply may spend one Attack, Scenario Short Skill. On a successful Normal WIP Roll, take D-Charges or roll on the Panoply Chart for a different weapon or item. Booty Troops and Troops with an applicable Skill need no WIP Roll.

After a successful acquisition the same Trooper cannot use that Panoply again. A rolled item already possessed can be rerolled. A Trooper in contact may instead spend one Short Skill to cancel their Unloaded State.

rules.name: Panoply Chart (D20)
paragraphs: 1–2: +1 ARM. 3–4: Light Flamethrower. 5–6: Grenades. 7–8: DA CC Weapon. 9: Multispectral Visor L1. 10: EXP CC Weapon.
11: Adhesive Launcher Rifle. 12: TAG—Immunity (AP); other Troop Types—+2 ARM. 13: Panzerfaust. 14: Monofilament CC Weapon. 15: MOV 8-4.
16: TAG—BS Attack (Shock); other Troop Types—MULTI Rifle. 17: MULTI Sniper Rifle. 18: TAG—Immunity (ARM); other Troop Types—+4 ARM. 19: Mimetism (-6). 20: TAG—BS Attack (+1B); other Troop Types—HMG.
The English and Spanish chart results are equivalent in concept, subject to the sources' normal unit conventions.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troops with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist-only tasks.

condition.text: If a player begins an Active Turn in Retreat!, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: Spanish p.53 expressly forbids targeting a Prototype with an Attack affecting another allied or enemy Trooper; English p.54 says only that Prototypes can be targeted.
English p.55 forbids any MODs to the attacker's CC Attribute against a Prototype; Spanish p.54 forbids positive CC Attribute MODs only.

English p.56 disqualifies capture while the carrier is in Silhouette contact with an enemy non-Null Model; Spanish p.55 has broader contact-with-enemy wording and excludes Null-state Models separately.

records.name: Outbreak
records.summary: Scan, stabilize, CivEvac and secure infected Civilians; the Alpha Infected is fixed at table center while four others and Stabilization Zones are placed by players.

condition.text: Score 1 Objective Point for each different Infected you have Scanned by game end, to a maximum of 3. Both players may Scan the same Infected, but each player may Scan it only once.
At game end, have Stabilized more Infected than your opponent. An Infected already Stabilized by one player cannot subsequently be Stabilized by the other.
At game end, be CivEvacing more Stabilized Infected than your opponent.
At game end, be CivEvacing the Stabilized Alpha Infected.
At game end, Secure at least one Infected that you have Stabilized or are CivEvacing, with no enemy non-Null Trooper within its Zone of Control.

rules.name: Infected Placement
paragraphs: Five Infected Civilians participate; the Alpha Infected is fixed at the table center. Before the Deployment Phase, each player places two further Infected entirely within the opponent's half of the table. Their locations are chosen by players, not pre-marked on the map.

Each player-placed Infected must be at least [[distance:4:inch]] outside the enemy Deployment Zone and at least [[distance:8:inch]] from all other Infected. They cannot be placed inside or atop scenery or buildings and must be in an accessible location.

The player who kept Deployment places both of their Infected first. A Trooper may CivEvac at most one Infected at a time. Infected are represented by suitable Infinity/Infinity Bootleg Models, normally HVT or Civilian miniatures.

It is not permitted to deploy in Silhouette contact with an Infected. The English and Spanish distance conventions differ slightly: [[distance:4:inch]] / [[distance:8:inch]] versus [[distance:10:cm]] / [[distance:20:cm]].

rules.name: Corner Deployment Zones
paragraphs: Side A and Side B deploy in opposite table corners in quarter-circle Deployment Zones whose radius depends on the number of Army Points. The diagram uses top-right for Side A and bottom-left for Side B.

rules.name: Player-Placed Stabilization Zones
paragraphs: There are two Circular Template Stabilization Zones ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter each), one placed by each player. After placing the Infected and before deployment, each player places one Template totally inside their own Deployment Zone on a surface large enough for the full Template.
The player who kept Deployment places the first Stabilization Zone. Its precise position is not specified by the published map and is not invented here.

At the end of each Player Turn, an Infected being CivEvaced is Stabilized if both the Infected and their CivEvacing Trooper are totally inside a Stabilization Zone. Mark which player Stabilized the Infected with a Player A or B Token.
An Infected already Stabilized by one player cannot be Stabilized by the other, including by a Stabilization Zone.

rules.name: Stabilize Infected (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic, or Specialist Operative may declare this Skill while in Silhouette contact with an Infected or an allied Trooper CivEvacing one.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Stabilize the Infected. On success mark it with the player's Token. Failed attempts may be repeated with another Short Skill.
restrictions: An Infected already Stabilized by the opponent cannot be Stabilized again.

paragraphs: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic or Specialist Operative may use this Attack, Scenario Short Skill while in Silhouette contact with an Infected or an allied Trooper CivEvacing one.

Make a Normal WIP Roll to Stabilize an Infected. On success, mark it with the player's Token. Failed Rolls can be retried using additional Short Skills; an Infected already Stabilized by the opponent cannot be Stabilized again.

rules.name: Scan Infected (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic, or Specialist Operative may Scan an Infected or Stabilized Infected in its Line of Fire and Zone of Control, whether or not the Infected is being CivEvaced.
effects: Declare an Attack, Scenario Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts can be repeated with another Short Skill.
restrictions: Each player may Scan a given Infected only once. The other player may Scan that Infected separately.

paragraphs: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic or Specialist Operative may Scan an Infected or Stabilized Infected that is within the Trooper's Line of Fire and Zone of Control, regardless of whether it is being CivEvaced.

Declare an Attack, Scenario Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed Rolls may be retried with further Short Skills. Each player may Scan any given Infected only once; the other player can independently Scan the same Infected.

rules.name: Doctor and Paramedic Bonus
paragraphs: Troopers with Doctor or Paramedic receive +1SD to the WIP Rolls required to Stabilize, Scan or perform CivEvac on an Infected. The source does not grant this bonus to Specialist Operatives without one of those Skills.

rules.name: Secure Infected
paragraphs: At game end, an Infected that you Stabilized or that one of your Troopers is CivEvacing is Secured if its Zone of Control contains no enemy Trooper in a non-Null State.

rules.name: No HVT or Classified Deck
paragraphs: No player deploys an HVT. The HVT Model and Secure HVT rules do not apply; the Classified Deck is not used and this scenario has no Classified Objectives.

condition.text: If a player begins an Active Turn in Retreat!, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: EN p.84 uses minimum [[distance:4:inch]] outside the enemy Deployment Zone and [[distance:8:inch]] between Infected; ES p.84 prints [[distance:10:cm]] and [[distance:20:cm]]. The metric values differ slightly from exact inch conversions, so both are disclosed rather than silently unified.

records.name: Critical Intervention
records.summary: Asymmetric Attacker/Defender mission to unlock and extract a Data Pack, secure the Server Room and overcome an optional automated defensive turret system.

condition.text: The Attacker has Unlocked the Data Console using the Inhibitor Antenna.
The Attacker successfully Extracted the Data Pack from the central Data Console.
At game end, the Trooper that Extracted the Data Pack is not considered Killed.
At game end, the Trooper that Extracted the Data Pack is in the Attacker's own Deployment Zone and is in a non-Null State.
At game end, the Attacker Dominates the Server Room Zone of Operations.
Kill at least 40 enemy Army Points in a 150-point game.
Kill at least 50 enemy Army Points in a 200-point game.
Kill at least 65 enemy Army Points in a 250-point game.
Kill at least 75 enemy Army Points in a 300-point game.
Kill at least 85 enemy Army Points in a 350-point game.
Kill at least 100 enemy Army Points in a 400-point game.
Prevent the Attacker from Unlocking the Data Console.
Prevent the Attacker from Extracting the Data Pack.
Kill the Trooper that Extracted the Data Pack. This award applies only if the Attacker Extracted the Pack.
At game end, the Defender Dominates the Server Room Zone of Operations.
Kill at least 75 enemy Army Points in a 150-point game.
Kill at least 100 enemy Army Points in a 200-point game.
Kill at least 125 enemy Army Points in a 250-point game.
Kill at least 150 enemy Army Points in a 300-point game.
Kill at least 175 enemy Army Points in a 350-point game.
Kill at least 200 enemy Army Points in a 400-point game.
Each player may complete one Classified Objective worth 1 Objective Point; instead they may select that card for INTELCOM Support and Control.

rules.name: Attacker and Defender Roles
paragraphs: Two fixed roles apply, not a mutually chosen Main Objective set: the player taking the first Player Turn is the Attacker, and the player taking the second Player Turn is the Defender. Each has distinct Main Objectives; the Classified Objective is common.

Before Deployment, the Defender may spend one Command Token either to activate the Server Room Defense System, or instead to ignore the Server Room deployment restriction and deploy up to 65 Army Points of Troops from their Army List anywhere within the Server Room. Superior Deployment Skills are not required for that exception.
This optional Command Token spending is additional to the Strategic Use of Command Tokens. The Defender may select only one of these options with the single Token.

rules.name: Deployment and Attacker Exclusion Zone
paragraphs: Both players deploy on opposite edges within the game-size-specific Deployment Zones. The Server Room is a No Deployment area unless the Defender spends the special Command Token on the room-deployment exception.

A central Exclusion Zone extends [[distance:4:inch]] on either side of the table's central line. Airborne Deployment (AD) or Superior Deployment Skills cannot be used to deploy inside that Zone; the source labels this as the Attacker's Exclusion Zone.

rules.name: Server Room and Gates
paragraphs: The Server Room is a central [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]] Zone of Operations (ZO). It is treated as having infinitely high walls completely blocking Line of Fire, with four Wide Gates, one in the center of each wall, open at game start.

Wide Gate Tokens or comparable scenery represent the Gates. Spanish p.100 explicitly confirms the Gates allow access irrespective of Silhouette Attribute. Neither publication defines a numeric Gate width to plot here; Gates are stated in these rules rather than invented on the SVG.
The Spanish publication describes the room as [[distance:20:cm]] × [[distance:20:cm]], slightly smaller than the English inches; geometry follows the English source.

rules.name: Dominate the Server Room ZO
paragraphs: The Server Room is Dominated by the player with more eligible Victory Points inside it. Models and Markers representing Troopers, as well as Proxies and Peripheral Troops, count; Null-state Troops, Mines, Deployable Repeaters, fake Holoechoes and other non-Trooper Tokens do not.

A Trooper is inside the ZO when more than half their base is inside. Shasvastii Troopers count in Shasvastii-Embryo or non-Null State under English p.100; Spanish p.100 instead specifies Normal or Unconscious.
Each non-Null Baggage Trooper inside the Server Room adds 20 Victory Points for this Domination comparison.

rules.name: Server Room Defense System
paragraphs: Two Armed Turrets (Defensive Turret A/B Tokens, or equivalent scenery/Models of the appropriate Silhouette) occupy separate corners inside the Server Room. Their diagram positions are schematic; no precise turret diameter or center-to-corner clearance is published.

When the Defense System is active, the Armed Turrets respond with BS Attack or CC Attack to Orders declared by the Attacker's active Models, not Markers, that are in their Line of Fire or Silhouette contact.

English p.101 lists an Armed Turret profile of CC 5, BS 10, WIP 11, ARM 2, BTS 3, STR 1 and Silhouette 2, with 360° Visor, Total Reaction, Combi Rifle and PARA CC Weapon (-3). MOV and PH have no printed values.

The Spanish p.101 table prints the STR-equivalent field as a dash, whereas English specifies STR 1. This is a source inconsistency; the English profile is recorded without fabricating a Spanish value.

rules.name: Data Console
paragraphs: A single 40 mm Data Console is fixed at the center of the Server Room, holding one Data Pack. It uses a Console A Token or scenery of the same diameter.

rules.name: Extract Data Pack (Attacker Only)

requirements: Only an Attacker Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Data Console may declare Extract Data Pack.
effects: Make a Normal WIP-6 Roll to Extract a Data Pack, placing a Token beside the successful Trooper. If the Data Console has been Unlocked, use a Normal WIP Roll without the -6 MOD. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.

paragraphs: Only an Attacker Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Data Console may declare the Attack, Scenario Short Skill Extract Data Pack.

Perform a Normal WIP-6 Roll to Extract the Data Pack, placing a Data Pack Token beside the successful Trooper. If the Data Console has been Unlocked, the Skill uses a Normal WIP Roll without the -6 MOD. Failure may be retried by spending another Short Skill.

rules.name: Data Pack Carrier
paragraphs: The Data Pack must be represented with its Token. Its carrier must always be on the table as a Model, never in a Marker State (such as Camouflage or Holoecho).
If the carrier enters Dead State after Extracting the Data Pack, remove the Data Pack Token. The scenario's objectives refer to the Trooper that Extracted the Pack.

rules.name: Inhibitor Antenna
paragraphs: One 40 mm Inhibitor Antenna is fixed next to an exterior corner of the Server Room in the Defender's table half, shown below the room's left corner in the source map. It may use a Transmission Antenna Token or equivalent scenery.

rules.name: Use Inhibitor Antenna (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Inhibitor Antenna may declare this Skill.
effects: Choose to Unlock the Data Console (Attacker only) or to activate/deactivate the Server Room Defense System (either side). A successful Normal WIP Roll performs that action. Failed attempts may be repeated, each spending another Short Skill.

paragraphs: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Inhibitor Antenna may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Choose one action: as the Attacker only, Unlock the Data Console; or as either side, activate or deactivate the Server Room Defense System.
A successful Normal WIP Roll performs the selected action. Failed attempts may be repeated, each spending another Short Skill.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist-only tasks.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: Troopers are considered Killed by the enemy when they enter Dead State, are in a Null State at game end, or were never deployed on the table as a Model or Marker by game end.

rules.name: INTELCOM Card (Support and Control)
paragraphs: Before the game begins, after choosing the initial Classified Objective, each player publicly declares whether that card is used as their Classified Objective or INTELCOM Card. Roll a die; the highest roll announces first. The card's mission text or numeric value remains Private Information.

At the end of the final Game Round, count points in Initiative order. A player with at least one non-Null Trooper inside the Server Room may use the INTELCOM Card in Support and Control Mode to add its numeric value to the Trooper-point total used for Zone of Operations control.
English p.103 describes adding the INTELCOM value to Victory Points inside a chosen ZO; Spanish p.104 says Army Points inside a ZO. Both are retained as source wording; no unrelated Zone is invented.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: Both EN pp.97-98 and ES pp.97-98 print a maximum Defender Main Objective total of 11 OP (1+3+2+3+2) plus 1 Classified OP, for 12 OP. The 12 printed OP are preserved and not silently normalized to a 10-point cap.

EN p.99 says [[distance:8:inch]] square for the Server Room, while ES p.99 says [[distance:20:cm]] square. The geometry uses English inches and records the near-equivalence without treating it as exact.
EN p.101 prints STR 1 on the Armed Turret Profile. ES p.101 shows a dash in its EST/STR column, not 1. Profile details are retained in rule text without resolving the discrepancy.

EN p.103 adds INTELCOM Support and Control value to Victory Points in the selected ZO. ES p.104 says Puntos de Ejército (Army Points), a terminology mismatch, not evidence of a different printed numeric value.
EN p.100 counts Shasvastii-Embryo or any non-Null State; ES p.100 specifies Normal or Unconscious. Keep each text's status wording distinct.
EN p.98 defines Exclusion half-width [[distance:4:inch]] while ES p.98 uses [[distance:10:cm]] for the same restricted area. They differ slightly in physical measurement.

records.name: CivEvac
records.summary: ITS Common Basic Short Skill (Optional, Scenario): take control of a Civilian with a WIP Roll and keep them in Silhouette contact while moving.

requirements: Only a Model can use CivEvac. A Marker declaring CivEvac is automatically revealed.
The Trooper must be in or reach Silhouette contact with the Civilian. The Civilian cannot have a CivEvac Token or be in Silhouette contact with an enemy Model.
The Trooper cannot already be CivEvacing two Civilians, possess Impetuous (including through Frenzy), possess Peripheral, be Troop Type REM or VH, perform a Coordinated Order, or be in a Fireteam.
effects: Pass a WIP+3 Roll to CivEvac the Civilian and place a CivEvac Token. A failed attempt may be retried by spending another Short Skill.
A CivEvaced Civilian stays in Silhouette contact with the controlling Trooper; position it in contact at the end of each movement. A Trooper may control at most two Civilians.
The Civilian remains on the table even if its controlling Trooper enters a Null State.
CivEvac automatically ends at the end of the Order if the controller becomes Isolated, Immobilized or Null, joins a Fireteam, becomes a Marker, or gains Impetuous. Remove the CivEvac Token.
The controller may voluntarily cancel CivEvac upon activation by an Order or ARO, without a Roll. Leave the Civilian on a horizontal table surface.
For a Hostile Civilian, the CivEvac WIP Roll does not receive the +3 MOD; identify that Civilian with a Hostile Token.
restrictions: CivEvac is an Optional, Scenario Common Skill; it is not a free movement or automatic civilian extraction.

records.name: Casevac
records.summary: ITS Optional Common Short Skill: carry an allied Stunned, Immobilized or Unconscious Trooper by entering Casevac State.

requirements: Only Models may declare Casevac; declaring it reveals any Marker.
The bearer must be in Silhouette contact with an allied Trooper in Stunned, Immobilized (IMM-A or IMM-B), or Unconscious State, unless a scenario rule modifies this.
The carrying Trooper must have PH at least equal to the carried Trooper's PH. A Trooper with Baggage ignores this PH requirement.
effects: Casevac activates [[state:casevac|Casevac State]] for the carrier and the carried allied Trooper. Its movement, ARO and cancellation effects are defined by that State.
restrictions: The carried Trooper cannot perform its own Orders or AROs while [[state:casevac|Casevac State]] applies.

records.name: Team-Ops
records.summary: Automatic Special Skill available only through the optional Team-Ops tournament Extra, allowing customization of a Team-Ops Trooper when creating an Army List.

requirements: The tournament Organizer must have selected the optional Team-Ops Extra.
An Army List using Team-Ops must include all three distinct Team-Ops Units: LI, HI and REM (or equivalents).
effects: During Army List creation, customize each Team-Ops Trooper's Unit Profile.
Select one normal Skill, Weapon or Equipment option, then choose one option from the Team-Ops Chart. Each Team-Ops Trooper must choose a different chart option.
restrictions: An Army List cannot include more than one Team-Ops group.
The optional Team-Ops Extra does not allow Infinity Spec-Ops; the group's composition may differ between a player's two tournament lists but cannot change during the tournament.

records.name: Request a Tacball
records.summary: Optional Attack Short Skill for Team-Ops Troopers in the second Game Round, placing a Tacball support drop without a Roll.

requirements: The requesting Trooper must have the Infinity Team-Ops Special Skill, available under the optional Team-Ops Extra.
The game must be in its second Game Round.
effects: Request a Tacball requires no Roll.
Place a 55 mm Tacball Token in Silhouette contact with any part of the Trooper's route, selecting its support item from the Tacball Chart when placing it.
At the end of that Order, the requesting Trooper applies the selected item. The Tacball Token remains until the end of the game, destruction or removal; it represents Deployable Equipment.
restrictions: Tacball chart items are unique and non-transferable.
Each player may use Request a Tacball only once per game.

records.name: Casevac State
records.summary: ITS Season 18 State entered through [[skill:casevac|Casevac]]: one Trooper carries an allied Stunned, Immobilized or Unconscious Trooper while moving in Silhouette contact.

requirements: Activate the State through [[skill:casevac|Casevac]]: a Model must be in Silhouette contact with an allied Trooper in Stunned, Immobilized (IMM-A or IMM-B) or Unconscious State, and have PH at least equal to the carried Trooper's PH, unless Baggage removes that PH requirement. Scenario rules may change the target requirement.
effects: The carrier and the carried Trooper activate together with a single Order or ARO and move simultaneously in Silhouette contact, using the carrier's MOV values.
The carried Trooper cannot declare or perform Orders or AROs; only the carrier declares and performs them.
Both Troopers provoke only one ARO from each eligible enemy within LoF or ZoC.
Template Weapon Attacks against either Trooper follow the Template Weapons Into Close Combat rule.
The carried Trooper does not block LoF and does not provide the +1 B MOD when engaging in Close Combat.
Casevac State is automatically cancelled if the carrier declares any Skill except Cautious Movement, Climb, Dodge, Jump, Reset or a Short Movement Skill.

Casevac State also ends if the carrier is activated in the Impetuous Phase, enters an Immobilized or Null State or another canceling State, or becomes a Marker (such as Camouflaged, Impersonation or Holoecho).
Casevac State automatically ends when the carried Trooper recovers from the Immobilized (IMM-A or IMM-B), Stunned or Unconscious State.
The carrier can voluntarily cancel Casevac State by spending a Short Skill of an Order, without a Roll.
restrictions: Unless a Scenario Special Rule says otherwise, a carrier cannot carry more than one Immobilized, Stunned or Unconscious Trooper at a time.
